result.title: Learning to Defer under Expert Drift
result.summary: The learning to defer (L2D) framework enables safety in machine learning and AI systems by allocating difficult or critical decisions to a human expert. However, most prior work on L2D assumes fixed expert reliability, overlooking temporal fluctuations in human performance due to factors such as fatigue and cognitive biases. Humans commonly exhibit such substantial, systematic performance shifts across a wide range of domains, from high-stakes settings such as radiology, aviation, and judicial decision-making, to everyday tasks such as crowdsourced image annotation. We propose Expert-Drift-Adapted Learning-to-Defer (EDA-L2D), a novel expert-aware L2D framework that explicitly models these temporal shifts by conditioning the deferral head on recent histories of expert outcomes via a sequence model. This history-aware approach enables adaptive deferral policies that anticipate reliability fluctuations and better allocate decisions between human and machine over time. We provide comprehensive experiments across three diverse tasks -- image classification, medical diagnosis, and hate speech detection -- including generalization analyses under realistic deferral conditions and irregular shifts in expert reliability. Our results show that EDA-L2D adapts more effectively than prior L2D methods to diverse temporal patterns of expert reliability, resulting in improved system performance and more effective deferral decisions. Code is available at https://github.com/ZiyaoMou/L2D-Expert-Drift.

AI.brief_summary: 论文指出既有 learning-to-defer 框架都假设专家可靠性固定，提出 EDA-L2D：用序列模型把 deferral head 条件化在近期专家结果历史上，以预测可靠性波动并动态分配人机决策，并在图像分类、医学诊断与仇恨言论检测三个任务上验证其对时间漂移的适应性。
AI.relevance_reason: 「何时交由外部专家」与 LVR 的 STOP 及证据获取决策结构相似，其基于历史结果序列估计可靠性变化的做法可能可供核查：能否类比为对视觉证据通道可靠性的在线估计，从而影响停止与再查询策略；但该文不涉及内部 latent 状态或视觉推理表示。
